newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL stocks seen mixed but blue chips could rebound.
newsitem.headline: KL stocks seen mixed but blue chips could rebound.

text.p: A digestion of recent gains mingled with selective buying could keep Kuala Lumpur shares in a mixed trading pattern, but dealers said they expect blue chips to resume an uptrend soon.
"I think overall it will be mixed," said an institutional dealer with a bank-linked brokerage firm. "There will be some play on the Composite Index."
News of a reshuffling in the ruling Malay party's supreme council is unlikely to have an impact on stocks, dealers said. On Thursday, the key Composite Index ended down 3.07 points to 1,231.10.

End-of-month orders could lift the market, dealers said. In any case, blue chips will almost certainly rise on Monday when banking and finance stocks Rashid Hussain, Maybank and DCB Holdings are requoted, they said.
"I think you're going to see the Composite Index fly on Monday, but to what extent it's difficult to say," said an institutional dealer with a local securities firm.
The three companies are included in a 2.16 billion ringgit bank merger announced earlier this week.
Elsewhere, palm oil concern Kwantas Corp is expected to list on Friday with a 2.95 ringgit offer price.
